name: Fibrous Green
lede: Fibrous Green is a vivid yellow-green matched to RAL 6039, the German industrial color standard, not a traditional dictionary-of-color name.

sections.title: An industrial standard, not a dictionary word
sections.body:
RAL, the German standards body founded in 1927, assigns this hue the code 6039 in its classic color collection [1]. Unlike Maerz and Paul's or Ridgway's dictionaries, RAL colors are specified for paint and industrial coatings rather than drawn from everyday naming; our hex value is an approximate screen rendering of that paint standard [1]. Our own classification places it in the region the ISCC-NBS would call vivid yellow green, Munsell notation 3.2GY 7.5/9.1 [2].

The nearest named colors on file are [[acid-green]], [[mustard-green]], [[oil-yellow]] and [[june-bud]], at 2.8, 4.8, 5.5 and 5.7 ΔE [2]. Its nearest library neighbor is a hue called Acid Green, and it sits between [[green]] and [[yellow]] on the color wheel [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This hue is rare in our archive of 23,781 paintings: a match within six units covers at least five percent of the canvas in only 3 of them, all from the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, as photographed [3]. All three are highlight-toned passages, including a 1910 still life of tulips and daisies [3]. A count this small cannot support a claim about any painter or period [3].
